column1: Air pollution is increasingly becoming the focus of government and citizen concern around the globe.
column2: 空气污染正日益成为全球政府和民众关注的焦点。

column1: From Mexico City and New York to Singapore and Tokyo, new solutions to this old problem are being proposed, Mailed and implemented with ever increasing speed.
column2: 从墨西哥城到纽约，从新加坡到东京，针对这一久存的问题，新的解决方案正被提出并迅速实施。

column1: It is feared that unless pollution reduction measures are able to keep pace with the continued pressures of urban growth, air quality in many of the world’s major cities will deteriorate beyond reason.
column2: 人们担心，如果减少污染的措施无法跟上城市发展的步伐，那么世界上许多主要城市的空气质量将会恶化到难以忍受的程度。

column1: Action is being taken along several fronts: through new legislation, improved enforcement and innovative technology.
column2: 正在从多个方面采取行动：通过新立法、加强执法和创新技术。

column1: In Los Angeles, state regulations are forcing manufacturers to try to sell ever cleaner cars: their first of the cleanest, titled “Zero Emission Vehicles’, have to be available soon, since they are intended to make up 2 per cent of sales in 1997.
column2: 在洛杉矶，州级法规迫使制造商不断推出更清洁的汽车。他们首款真正意义上的‘零排放车辆’即将上市，因为这些汽车计划在1997年的销量中占据2%。

column1: Local authorities in London are campaigning to be allowed to enforce anti-pollution laws themselves; at present only the police have the power to do so, but they tend to be busy elsewhere.
column2: 伦敦的当地政府正在努力争取拥有自行执行环保法律的权力；目前只有警察有权这么做，不过他们往往忙于处理其他事务，无暇顾及这一事项。

column1: In Singapore, renting out road space to users is the way of the future.
column2: 在新加坡，将道路空间出租给使用者是未来的趋势。

column1: When Britain’s Royal Automobile Club monitored the exhausts of 60,000 vehicles, it found that 12 per cent of them produced more than half the total pollution.
column2: 当英国皇家汽车俱乐部对6万辆车辆的尾气进行监测时，发现其中12%的车辆产生的污染量超过了总数的一半。

column1: Older cars were the worst offenders; though a sizeable number of quite new cars were also identified as gross polluters, they were simply badly tuned.
column2: 使用年限较长的汽车是最严重的污染源；虽然也有不少新款汽车被认定为严重污染源，但问题主要出在汽车调校不当。

column1: California has developed a scheme to get these gross polluters off the streets: they offer a flat $700 for any old, run-down vehicle driven in by its owner.
column2: 加利福尼亚州已经制定了一项计划，旨在让这些造成严重污染的车辆从道路上消失：对于由车主自行驾驶的老旧破旧车辆，政府提供700美元的补偿金。

column1: The aim is to remove the heaviest-polluting, most decrepit vehicles from the roads.
column2: 目标是将污染最严重且已老旧不堪的车辆从道路上清除出去。

column1: As part of a European Union environmental programme, a London council is testing an infra-red spectrometer from the University of Denver in Colorado.
column2: 作为欧盟环保计划的一部分，伦敦的一个地方委员会正在测试来自科罗拉多州丹佛大学的红外光谱仪。

column1: It gauges the pollution from a passing vehicle – more useful than the annual stationary rest that is the British standard today – by bouncing a beam through the exhaust and measuring what gets blocked.
column2: 它通过将一束光射入尾气中并测量被阻挡的部分，来检测过往车辆的污染程度——这种方法比目前英国采用的年度静止检测标准更实用。

column1: The council’s next step may be to link the system to a computerised video camera able to read number plates automatically.
column2: 该委员会的下一步行动可能是将该系统与一种能够自动读取车牌号码的计算机化摄像装置相连。

column1: The effort to clean up cars may do little to cut pollution if nothing is done about the tendency to drive them more.
column2: 如果无法改变人们更倾向于驾驶汽车的习惯，那么仅改善汽车本身的努力对减少污染可能作用有限。

column1: Los Angeles has some of the world’s cleanest cars – far better than those of Europe – but the total number of miles those cars drive continues to grow.
column2: 洛杉矶拥有世界上一些最清洁的汽车，其环保性能远胜于欧洲的汽车，但这些汽车行驶的总英里数仍在持续增长。

column1: One solution is car-pooling, an arrangement in which a number of people who share the same destination share the use of one car.
column2: 一种解决方案是拼车，即多名有相同目的地的人共同使用一辆车。

column1: However, the average number of people in a car on the freeway in Los Angeles, which is 1.0, has been falling steadily.
column2: 然而，洛杉矶高速公路上每辆车的平均乘客数量正持续下降，目前为1.0人。

column1: Increasing it would be an effective way of reducing emissions as well as easing congestion.
column2: 提高空气污染水平将有效减少排放并缓解交通拥堵。

column1: The trouble is, Los Angelenos seem to like being alone in their cars.
column2: 问题是，洛杉矶人似乎喜欢独自坐在车里。

column1: Singapore has for a while had a scheme that forces drivers to buy a badge if they wish to visit a certain part of the city.
column2: 新加坡曾有一项政策，要求司机若想进入城市某区域，必须购买通行证。

column1: Electronic innovations make possible increasing sophistication: rates can vary according to road conditions, time of day and so on.
column2: 电子创新使得技术日益复杂：速率会因道路状况、时间等因素而变化。

column1: Singapore is advancing in this direction, with a city-wide network of transmitters to collect information and charge drivers as they pass certain points.
column2: 新加坡正在朝着这个方向迈进，整个城市都配备了发射器网络，用于收集信息，并在驾驶员经过特定地点时向他们收费。

column1: Such road-pricing, however, can be controversial.
column2: 不过，这种道路定价方式可能会引发争议。

column1: When the local government in Cambridge, England, considered introducing Singaporean techniques, it faced vocal and ultimately successful opposition.
column2: 在英格兰的剑桥市，当地政府在考虑引入新加坡技术时，遭遇了强烈且最终成功的反对。

column1: The scope of the problem facing the world’s cities is immense.
column2: 世界上的城市所面临的问题非常严峻，其范围极其广泛。

column1: In 1992, the United Nations Environmental Programme and the World Health Organisation (WHO) concluded that all of a sample of twenty megacities – places likely to have more than ten million inhabitants in the year 2000 – already exceeded the level the WHO deems healthy in at least one major pollutant.
column2: 在1992年，联合国环境规划署和世界卫生组织宣布，在选取的20个大城市中，至少有1个城市在至少一个主要污染物指标上超过了世界卫生组织所认为的健康标准。这些城市的人口预计在2000年时将超过1000万。

column1: Two-thirds of them exceeded the guidelines for two, seven for three or more.
column2: 其中三分之二的项目超过了两项标准，七项超过了三项或更多。

column1: Of the six pollutants monitored by the WHO – carbon dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, sulphur dioxide, lead and particulate matter – it is this last category that is attracting the most attention from health researchers.
column2: 在世界卫生组织监测的六种污染物——二氧化碳、二氧化氮、臭氧、二氧化硫、铅和颗粒物中，颗粒物这一类别正引起健康研究人员最多的关注。

column1: PM10, a sub-category of particulate matter measuring ten-millionths of a metre across, has been implicated in thousands of deaths a year in Britain alone.
column2: PM10是一种颗粒物子类别，其直径仅为百万分之一米，仅在英国，这种颗粒物就导致了数千人死亡。

column1: Research being conducted in two counties of Southern California is reaching similarly disturbing conclusions concerning this little-understood pollutant.
column2: 在南加州两个县进行的研究正得出了关于这种尚不为人所理解的污染物的相似令人不安的结论。
column11: little-understood|adj. 尚不为人所理解的

column1: A world-wide rise in allergies, particularly asthma, over the past four decades is now said to be linked with increased air pollution.
column2: 在过去四十年里，全球范围内过敏症尤其是哮喘的发病率上升，这一现象被认为与空气污染的增加有关。

column1: The lungs and brains of children who grow up in polluted air offer further evidence of its destructive power the old and ill; however, are the most vulnerable to the acute effects of heavily polluted stagnant air.
column2: 在污染严重的空气中成长的儿童，他们的肺部和大脑都受到了严重的损害。这些孩子更容易受到严重污染空气带来的急性伤害，尤其是那些年老或身体虚弱的人。

column1: It can actually hasten death, so it did in December 1991 when a cloud of exhaust fumes lingered over the city of London for over a week.
column2: 空气污染实际上会加速死亡，1991年12月，伦敦上空持续弥漫着废气烟雾超过一周。

column1: The United Nations has estimated that in the year 2000 there will be twenty-four mega-cities and a further eighty-five cities of more than three million people.
column2: 联合国估计，到2000年将有24个特大城市和另外85个超过300万人的城市。

column1: The pressure on public officials, corporations and urban citizens to reverse established trends in air pollution is likely to grow in proportion with the growth of cities themselves.
column2: 公众官员、企业及城市居民对逆转空气污染趋势的压力，可能随着城市自身的发展而增长。

column1: Progress is being made.
column2: 正在取得进展。

column1: The question, though, remains the same: ‘Will change happen quickly enough?’
column2: 不过，问题依然相同：变化能否发生得足够迅速呢？
